code:
NOT TRUE
= (λb. b FALSE TRUE) (λx.λy. x)
->β (λx.λy. x) FALSE TRUE
->β (λy. FALSE) TRUE
->β FALSE  OK
description: This reduction uses a Church boolean as a selector to negate TRUE.

steps.description: NOT applies its boolean argument to FALSE and TRUE. The argument here is the Church encoding of TRUE.
Substituting TRUE for b makes TRUE select its first argument, FALSE.

steps.answer: It returns FALSE, its first captured argument.
steps.question: What does the remaining lambda return after it receives TRUE?

steps.description: The final beta reduction leaves FALSE. The encoding therefore negates TRUE.

title: Reduce NOT TRUE
